hook: SCP-7777 starts as a puzzle about random number generators and turns into an institutional thriller. The access warning at the very top is worth keeping in mind as you go. Pay attention to which names keep showing up in the instance log; this is an article that rewards close reading.
whyItMatters: It casts the Ethics Committee, RAISA, the Overseers and the Chaos Insurgency as players in a single power struggle, which is why its tag list is so crowded with staff and organization names. The core device, an anomaly that exposes wrongdoing, lets the article ask who inside the Foundation actually holds anyone to account. Footnotes point to other numbered files, so it feels embedded in the wider wiki rather than standalone.
thingsToNotice: The early instances play like a case-of-the-week format, which lowers your guard. Small recurring details, such as one technician repeatedly being the one who finds the messages, and footnotes about altered records, quietly build a second story under the first. The closing memo reframes the whole anomaly and then pivots again, so no faction comes out looking clean. Note that the final speaker treats the file itself as a tool, which leaves the reader feeling recruited into the next scheme.

related.note: Cited in a footnote; another generator whose randomness gives way to readable sentences.
